 McLean Homeowners Charged Following Large Underage Drinking Party
 By FCPD Public Affairs Bureau · November 12, 2026 
 McLean Police District – Officers from our McLean District Station have charged two homeowners following a large party involving hundreds of teenagers, underage drinking, fireworks, and disorderly conduct at a McLean residence.
 On November 6 at approximately 9:03 p.m., officers responded to the 1400 block of Woodacre Drive after multiple 911 callers reported a large party that had gotten out of control. Callers estimated that between 100 and 300 people had gathered at the residence.
 Upon arrival, officers encountered a large crowd and fireworks being discharged. Officers worked to restore order and safely disperse those gathered at the residence.
 Through their investigation, officers determined the homeowners, Lisa Vaughan, 45, and Aubrey Vaughan, 55, both of McLean, had organized the party for their teenage child.
 Following the investigation, officers obtained warrants charging both Lisa and Aubrey Vaughan with Contributing to the Delinquency of a Minor and Maintaining a Common Nuisance. Both homeowners later turned themselves in at the Fairfax County Adult Detention Center where they were released on $1,000 unsecured bonds each.
 This incident serves as a reminder of the importance of safety and supervision when hosting gatherings involving minors. While these events are often intended to be fun and enjoyable, circumstances can change quickly. We encourage parents and homeowners to remain mindful of activities taking place on their property, take steps to prevent underage drinking, and contact police if concerns arise or a situation begins to escalate.
